baseline.public_policy: The stable public URL may serve an Admin-directed unverified development build when explicitly authorized. Independent Tester verification remains required before a build or phase is described as independently verified under normal autonomous progression.

phase_policy.origin_rule: Every new campaign begins at authoritative world coordinate (0,0) in the SEED-generated inhabited starting village, with the initial playable view centered on the campaign origin.
phase_policy.map_rule: Every cumulative phase must preserve and progressively extend the persistent living strategic world map as the primary playable surface. The visible tile region is only a local active part of the larger continuous world, not a finite complete map.
phase_policy.world_generation_rule: Compatible SEED + world coordinates + compatible generator rules reproduce the same unmodified base world. Base composition includes coherent terrain/water/roads/bridges, settlement archetype foundations, local populations, habitat/ecology foundations and, where political organization applies, coherent base realm/country, region/province, territorial/border relationships and settlement-affiliation identity. Neighboring regions remain deterministic and available without a gameplay-defined outer boundary.
phase_policy.political_geography_rule: The SEED defines reproducible base political geography as part of the same physical world rather than disconnected labels: realm/country and region/province identity, settlement affiliation and territorial relationships should be spatially coherent with terrain, water, routes, settlements and neighboring regions. Campaign history may later change ownership, borders, affiliations, capitals or realm composition; those authoritative changes refine/override the unchanged base without rewriting the SEED.
phase_policy.settlement_evolution_rule: Settlements have authoritative historical development state rather than frozen templates. Campaign time and simulation outcomes may support stability, growth, contraction, damage, recovery, fortification, functional change, abandonment, ruin or repopulation. Detailed materialization must reflect accumulated development state instead of silently resetting to the untouched SEED template.
phase_policy.persistence_rule: Deterministic unchanged base-world content, including unchanged base political geography, may be regenerated from SEED and coordinates; authoritative campaign changes are persisted. Current-world reconstruction composes SEED base state, authoritative fantasy campaign date/time, applicable hierarchical/off-screen progression including settlement development and political history, and saved persistent changes.
phase_policy.real_time_rule: The campaign is real-time rather than turn-based. At normal speed 60 real-world minutes equal one 24-hour in-game day, so one in-game hour equals 2.5 real-world minutes.
phase_policy.calendar_origin_rule: A new campaign fantasy chronology is initialized from accepted real-world civil date/time at creation: fantasy day and month numbers and time-of-day equal the real-world origin, while fantasy year = real-world year - 2000. Example: 28.08.2026 14:30 -> 28.08.0026 14:30. The initial game time is therefore not fixed at 06:00.
phase_policy.calendar_continuity_rule: The real-world creation mapping is only the synchronization origin. After creation, fantasy campaign chronology remains its own accelerated authoritative timeline and must not be directly remapped to current civil date/time on launch. Accepted real-world elapsed time advances that established chronology at normal speed: one real-world hour = one in-game day, 24 real hours = 24 in-game days, and 10 real days = 240 in-game days, using bounded catch-up rather than replaying every missed tick.
phase_policy.day_night_rule: Authoritative game time defines dawn/daylight transition at 05:00 and darkness/night transition at 22:00. Moving physically accurate shadows are not required.
phase_policy.simulation_fidelity_rule: The protagonist's active/relevant region uses continuous high-detail simulation; inactive regions use lower-cost authoritative elapsed-time progression/aggregation rather than freezing or full-detail ticking.
phase_policy.hierarchical_simulation_rule: The same authoritative world may be represented at progressively different resolution from global/world through realm/country, region, settlement and local active layers. Compact higher-level state preserves large-scale causality, settlement-development history and political/territorial state without materializing all local entities.
phase_policy.lazy_materialization_rule: Unvisited or inactive detailed state is materialized only when relevant from compatible SEED base state, coordinates, authoritative fantasy campaign date/time, accumulated hierarchical outcomes including settlement-development and political-geography history, persistent changes and local rules; visit/render order must not become authority.
phase_policy.strategic_scale_view_rule: As protagonist authority expands, regional, realm/country and wider-world strategic views must summarize authoritative aggregate state and evolving political geography from the same living world rather than create disconnected dashboard truth.
phase_policy.npc_life_rule: NPC routines may be time-aware and role/location dependent; simple varied deterministic/Local-BOT ambient NPC-to-NPC dialogue may respond to profession, settlement/location, environment, time and relevant local conditions without becoming authoritative truth by itself.
phase_policy.ecology_rule: Domestic/farm animals, wildlife and a broad original medieval-fantasy bestiary are SEED/habitat/context-aware simulation-backed world content where gameplay-relevant.
phase_policy.designer_rule: Every phase requires at least one independently testable Designer-role task before normal phase completion.
phase_policy.normal_phase_transition_rule: Under normal autonomous progression, an independent Worker acting in the Tester role must independently pass the active phase gate before the next phase activates. The Tester must not approve work produced by the same Worker identity. Explicit Admin instructions may override normal publication or phase/release workflow requirements without converting unverified work into verified work.
